articles.title: NFL Catchup: Rams Name Ty Simpson QB3; Cardinals Extend WR Michael Wilson
articles.summary: Here's the latest NFL news around the league on Thursday.
articles.body: At long last, the NFL season is right around the corner. We are less than a week away from kickoff, and as initial 53-man depth charts take shape, final roster moves and tactical shifts are making noise across the league. The Los Angeles Rams officially revealed their Week 1 depth chart, listing rookie Ty Simpson as the third-string quarterback. Meanwhile, the NFC West news gets even more intriguing with the Arizona Cardinals agreeing to a massive multi-year extension with wide receiver Michael Wilson. Staying in the NFC, the Chicago Bears are managing practice injuries with wide receiver Rome Odunze and running back D'Andre Swift. Following that, it turns out New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo briefly considered retirement while recovering from last year's season-ending ankle injury. Here's the latest NFL news around the league on Thursday. Simpson Will Start Season As QB3 After a strong preseason showing, the Los Angeles Rams have released their depth chart for the start of the 2026 season. With Week 1 on the way, head coach Sean McVay has opted for Stetson Bennett as Matthew Stafford’s backup quarterback. That means Ty Simpson, who the team took with the 13th overall pick in April's draft, will be the third-string quarterback. The Rams had been adamant about Simpson sitting and learning this season, especially as Stafford nears the end of his career. Stafford's timeline remains uncertain, but he has been at the center of retirement rumors over the last couple of years. Simpson and Bennett were in lockstep all camp, but Bennett ultimately took the edge. After watching both get extensive preseason reps, McVay appears to agree, favoring Bennett for the backup job. "Stetson Bennett being named the No. 2 QB by the Rams over Ty Simpson should not be surprising," our Eric D. Williams noted. "He was clearly the better player during training camp. But Simpson showed steady improvement." The Rams are set to head to Australia to face off against the NFC West division rival San Francisco 49ers for Week 1. Cardinals, Wilson Agree To 3-Year Extension The Arizona Cardinals reached an agreement Thursday on a three-year contract extension with wide receiver Michael Wilson, according to reports from ESPN and NFL Network. The deal keeps the 26-year-old receiver under contract with the franchise through the 2029 season. Originally selected by Arizona in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Stanford, Wilson has established himself as a primary target in the Cardinals' offense alongside Trey McBride. Wilson is expected to officially sign the contract on Thursday ahead of Arizona's regular-season opener against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sept. 13. Skattebo Considered Retirement After Ankle Injury New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo shared that he briefly considered retiring from the NFL after suffering a severe ankle injury last year. Skattebo, who suffered a dislocated ankle, open tibia fracture, and ruptured deltoid ligament in Week 8, shared during an appearance on "Up & Adams" that he contemplated stepping away about a month into his rehabilitation. "The first month was kind of like, ‘Damn, do I really want to do this?’" Skattebo said. "I think [the injury] gave me an extra step of finding that deep place and coming out of a hole that I didn't know I could come out of. I'm appreciative of it, and I'm excited to see what I can build on it." Skattebo noted he had a personal rule in college to retire if he suffered a major injury, but ultimately decided to return after showing promise over seven full games as a rookie. Before the injury, he compiled 410 rushing yards, 207 receiving yards, and seven total touchdowns. The second-year back returned to the field during the preseason on Aug. 15 and is projected to lead a Giants backfield rotation that features Najee Harris, Tyrone Tracy Jr., and Devin Singletary. Odunze, Swift Sidelined At Bears Practice The Chicago Bears had a pair of injury scares right before Week 1. Wide receiver Rome Odunze and running back D'Andre Swift were both reportedly sidelined during practice Thursday. According to reports, Odunze exited with a member of the training staff near the beginning of practice and appeared to be dealing with a right leg or foot injury. Odunze, who missed five games last season with a foot fracture, enters the 2026 campaign expected to serve as Chicago's top receiver alongside Luther Burden III following the offseason trade of DJ Moore. Swift's injury reportedly occurred near the end of practice during a full-team drill. With backup Kyle Monangai currently sidelined with a hyperextended knee, Swift's exit leaves Chicago's running back room rather thin heading into the holiday weekend. Injury News & Notes

articles.title: AFC South Predictions: Can The Texans Reclaim The Division From The Jaguars?
articles.summary: Who'll win the AFC South? Here's who the "First Things First" crew thinks will win the division crown.
articles.body: The AFC South is shaping up to be one of the NFL's most unpredictable divisions this season. The Houston Texans have held the crown for years, but can they reclaim the division with the Jacksonville Jaguars' young core not going away any time soon? With a healthy Daniel Jones back for the Indianapolis Colts and veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen now in the fold, the Colts could make some real noise. Over in Tennessee, the arrival of Robert Saleh puts a rebuilding Titans team in a prime position to play spoiler down the stretch. If you want to know how the AFC South will unfold, the "First Things First" group of co-hosts were all over it. On Thursday’s show, Nick Wright, Danny Parkins, and Chris Broussard broke down the AFC South. They didn't stop at general commentary, either. The trio made their definitive predictions for how the division will shake out. Nick Wright's AFC South Prediction 1.Houston Texans 2.Jacksonville Jaguars 3.Indianapolis Colts 4.Tennessee Titans The Titans are entering a full rebuild under head coach Robert Saleh, but Nick Wright still sees potential for growth. With offensive additions like Carnell Tate and Wan’Dale Robinson, Wright believes a six-win season is well within reach. "I do have them getting six wins … here’s the case for them," Wright said. "Carnell Tate, Cam Ward take a year or two jump, and maybe Robert Saleh is actually a good head coach." When it comes to the expectations for the Colts, all eyes shift towards Jones and his recovery from the season-ending Achilles injury. Wright’s concerns aren't about Jones specifically, but they’re focused squarely on head coach Shane Steichen. After failing to meet expectations, Wright believes Steichen should be firmly on the hot seat. "Daniel Jones [is] quickly coming back from the Achilles injury, but how mobile is he actually going to be," Wright said. Also, I worry about Shane Steichen, and I worry about the instant hot seat." When it comes to the Jaguars, they're not so easy to predict. After winning 13 games last season and winning the division, they could be a team that's not just on the rise, but could be competitive for years to come. Wright made sure to highlight the Jaguars' young core in quarterback Trevor Lawrence and two-way standout Travis Hunter. "13 wins like last year," Wright said. "There’s no way they don’t get at least a little more out of Travis Hunter this year. They’re not going to get less. Year two of Trevor Lawrence and [Liam] Coen…I like that. They have, far away, the best quarterback in that division." The Houston Texans topped Wright's predictions. He highlighted that the performance of quarterback C.J. Stroud will be a large factor in Houston's success this season. "I think they will be fighting for the No. 1 seed all year," Wright said. "I think they go 12-5. If CJ Stroud is average, they can win 11 games. If he's above average, they can win 12 games. If he's good, you can argue they're the best team in the league." Chris Broussard's AFC South Prediction 1.Houston Texans 2.Jacksonville Jaguars 3.Indianapolis Colts 4.Tennessee Titans Broussard followed Wright's lead in his AFC South predictions, with the Texans standing at No. 1 and the Titans at the bottom. With new head coach Robert Saleh, Broussard is hoping for good things to come out of Saleh's first year and Ward's second starting season. "I hope I'm wrong. I like Cam Ward. I would really like to see him do something this year," Broussard said. "I'd like to see Saleh get a real chance … We'll see, I'm pulling for him." For the Colts' third-place prediction, Broussard has a hard time believing that Indianapolis won't follow the same pattern this season as it did last season. "We all remember the 8-2 start, and then one of the worst collapses in NFL history. They lost their last seven. They lost their last three when Jones was healthy. Why? Because they started playing good teams," Broussard said. For the Jaguars at second, their run to the playoffs was impressive, but Broussard does not see back-to-back appearances. "At No. 2, the Jags, but missing the playoffs," Broussard said. "He was very good last year. Is that who he finally is? Or is he going to go back down the roller coaster? I'm not betting on a bad year, but I'm not expecting a good year." As the Texans top Broussard's list, the talented defense is a large factor in its success. However, the talent that Stroud brings to the offense will be another point of focus for Broussard. "The Houston Texans [are] winning this division. Contrary to popular opinion, C.J. was average last year … obviously he was banged up for a few games. I expect a bounce back," Broussard said. "I don't know if I'm ever expecting him to be that great top-five quarterback that we thought he was going to be." Danny Parkins' AFC South Prediction 1.Indianapolis Colts 2.Houston Texans 3.Jacksonville Jaguars 4.Tennessee Titans Like Wright and Broussard, Danny Parkins placed the Titans in last. Parkins did not hold back when it came to what the Titans season could look like under quarterback Cam Ward. "I'd be really worried if I was a Titans fan. I love Carnell Tate, I loved it leading up to the NFL Draft," Parkins said. "I didn't see much of anything to believe in Cam Ward. I think they are in contention, with the Dolphins, for the worst team in the NFL." Parkins switched things up and placed the Jaguars third. While Lawrence has been through ups and downs in his NFL career, Parkins is not expecting Lawrence to hold the same standard he did in last year's 13-4 season. "A huge regression for the Jacksonville Jaguars," Parkins said. "I think Trevor Lawrence cannot be trusted. Is it possible that Liam Coen unlocked it? Absolutely. … He did it with Baker, he did it with Trevor. But his whole career has been a roller-coaster. Seems like we might be ready for a big dip." As for Parkins' second-place team, the Texans, the defense should not be an issue for Houston. However, the concern lies within Stroud at the helm of the offense. "You have the best defense in the NFL, but defensive production year over year does fluctuate," Parkins said. They had remarkable defensive health last year … I don't have evidence that C.J. Stroud is good." And sitting atop his AFC South predictions, Parkins believes the Colts will take home the AFC South title. Parkins emphasized the Colts could be a dangerous team in the division if Jones is back in full force. "They return four of five starters on their offensive line. … I really like their offense this year … they need to win by scoring," Parkins said. "So if you see the best version of Daniel Jones for a full year, I think the Colts can win the AFC South."

articles.title: How to Watch Fresno State vs. USC: TV Channel, Live Stream, Time

articles.body: The Fresno State Bulldogs visit the USC Trojans on Friday, September 4, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. PT from Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Los Angeles, CA. USC enters Friday off a 42-26 win over San Jose State to open the 2026 season, improving to 1-0 as the No. 14 team in the country. Fresno State is still 0-0 on the year, and its last trip to face USC ended in a 45-17 loss back in 2022. USC is a 21.5-point favorite at DraftKings, with the total set at 51.5. Below, we'll give you all the details you need to know about how to watch this game. How to Watch Fresno State vs. USC Players to Watch Jayden MaiavaQBUSC Trojans USC needed one week to answer questions about its passing game, and Maiava provided it. He threw for 286 yards and two touchdowns in the opener, added a rushing score, and finished with 18 points as the Trojans built the nation's top third down offense right out of the gate. Lincoln Riley's attack already ranks first in the country in third down conversion rate and total yards per game, and Maiava is the one steering it. Fresno State's defense carried that program through a nine win season a year ago, but it has not faced a quarterback playing at this pace yet. If Maiava is as efficient in Week 2 as he was in Week 1, USC's offense could turn this into a rout early. Trent MosleyWRUSC Trojans Mosley did more than catch passes in USC's opener. He led the Trojans with 118 receiving yards and a touchdown, then added 56 punt return yards to finish with a team high 174 all purpose yards. That versatility matters against a Fresno State team built around defense, since Mosley does not need a shootout to be effective. He can change field position on special teams even on a night when the passing game stalls. With Maiava spreading throws around a deep receiver room, Mosley's ability to win after the catch gives USC a release valve, whether the Trojans are grinding through Fresno State's toughest defensive series or trying to put the game away early. Khristian MartinQBFresno State Bulldogs Fresno State opens the season still sorting out its quarterback room, and Martin is one of two candidates coach Matt Entz has trusted with the job, along with Jayden Mandal. Whichever one starts against USC will lean on a defense that carried the Bulldogs to nine wins a year ago, since Fresno State's only Power Four loss in 2025 came by 24 points to Kansas. Martin does not have to be spectacular for Fresno State to hang in this game. He needs to protect the ball, extend drives and let a defense that already outplays its own offense control the tempo. Against a USC team that scored at will in Week 1, that margin for error will be thin. articles.title: How to Watch Toledo vs. Michigan State: TV Channel, Live Stream, Time
articles.summary: Learn which TV channel or how to live stream the CFB Week 1 Toledo Rockets and Michigan State Spartans game.
articles.body: The Toledo Rockets visit the Michigan State Spartans on Friday, September 4, 2026 at 8:00 p.m. ET from Spartan Stadium, East Lansing, MI. Michigan State and Toledo both enter Friday night's opener at 0-0. Toledo averaged 30.8 points per game in 2025, well ahead of Michigan State's 24.6, a track record the Rockets bring into Spartan Stadium. Michigan State is a 9.5-point favorite at DraftKings, with the total set at 47.5. Below, we'll give you all the details you need to know about how to watch this game. How to Watch Toledo vs. Michigan State Players to Watch Andrew ZockEDGEToledo Rockets Zock is the marquee addition in new coach Mike Jacobs' haul of 21 small-school transfers, and he arrives with a real track record. He picked up 20 tackles for loss and 11.5 sacks last season as the Southern Conference's Defensive Player of the Year, numbers that would have led most Group of Five defenses outright. Toledo is chasing its third Mid-American Conference title game in five years, and Jacobs is 33-8 combining his last three seasons at Mercer and Lenoir-Rhyne. None of that translates automatically to the MAC, but a pass rusher who racked up that kind of production against lesser competition gives Toledo's front seven a proven disruptor from the jump. Michigan State's rebuilt offensive line will be the first real measuring stick. Cam EdwardsRBMichigan State Spartans Michigan State overhauled its roster hoping transfers could speed up a rebuild, and Edwards gives the offense a proven workhorse. He rushed for 1,240 yards at UConn last year and enters this season as the fourth-leading returning rusher in the nation with 2,690 career rushing yards over 36 games. New coach Pat Fitzgerald inherited a senior class heavy with new names, and Edwards is the one piece opposing defenses already have to prepare for. Toledo enters with a defense built around transfer additions of its own, led by edge rusher Andrew Zock, so neither team is hiding from how much roster turnover shaped this opener. If Edwards can run against a defense that new, Michigan State's offense has a real foundation to build on. Alessio MilivojevicQBMichigan State Spartans Every new face at Michigan State arrived through the transfer portal this off-season, except Milivojevic, who remains the same quarterback who threw 10 touchdowns against just three interceptions a season ago. That continuity matters against a Toledo defense that will lean on newcomers of its own to slow down the Spartans. Fitzgerald's rebuild depends on Milivojevic protecting the ball while Edwards and a retooled defense find their footing, and his low interception rate a year ago suggests he can do exactly that. Toledo's own quarterback situation is far less settled, which puts extra pressure on Milivojevic to be the steady half of this matchup rather than the swing factor. Purdue's defense gave up plenty a year ago during a 2-10 season, and while a Missouri Valley Conference team walking into Ross-Ade Stadium is still a significant step up in competition, Wuest's early versatility at least gives Indiana State a specific answer for how it plans to move the ball. He threw for 300 yards or more twice a year ago, including a 30 of 50, 302 yard effort against a top 25 ranked Illinois team, proof that his arm can handle high volume against real competition. Coach Barry Odom's Boilermakers have not beaten a Big Ten opponent since a November 2023 win over Indiana, of all teams, which will feel especially strange now that the Hoosiers are the reigning national champions. An opener against an FCS opponent in Indiana State is exactly the kind of low-risk environment where Browne needs to look sharp before Purdue's Big Ten grind begins. articles.title: World Chess Championship: Sindarov keeps Gukesh showdown on hold, says preparation starts after Olympiad
articles.summary: Chess News: Javokhir Sindarov knows the biggest challenge of his young career awaits later this year when he takes on defending champion D Gukesh for the world cr.
articles.body: Javokhir Sindarov knows the biggest challenge of his young career awaits later this year when he takes on defending champion D Gukesh for the world crown. But the Uzbek prodigy is refusing to let the much-anticipated showdown dominate his thoughts just yet.Sindarov will face fellow 20-year-old Gukesh in a 14-game World Championship match in Geneva from November 24 to December 12. Yet, rather than beginning his specific preparations for the title clash immediately, the Candidates winner is keeping his attention on the tournaments directly ahead."Right now, I'm focusing on my next events -- the Global Chess League and the Olympiad. After those, I will start preparing for the World Championship match," Sindarov, who will represent Fyers American Gambits in the fourth edition of the GCL, said during a media interaction.Sindarov wants to face Gukesh at his bestSindarov's approach also reflects his unwillingness to read too much into Gukesh's recent results. The Indian world champion has endured an inconsistent period since winning the title in 2024, but Sindarov believes that will have little bearing on their eventual battle."Gukesh is very strong. I played with him a few times and I really feel he is a very strong chess player," Sindarov said. "I cannot say a lot of things before the match. I just want to play my good chess and enjoy it."That measured approach comes after a remarkable year for Sindarov. He earned his world title shot by winning the Candidates Tournament with a round to spare, producing a dominant campaign that included four consecutive victories against elite opposition. He has since continued to establish himself among the leading players of the new generation.Immediate focus on GCL and OlympiadBefore Geneva, Sindarov has the fourth season of the Global Chess League in Bengaluru from September 5 to 13, followed by the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand from September 15 to 27.His preparations for the World Championship will be overseen by coach Roman Vidonyak. Sindarov has indicated that the detailed work for Gukesh will begin only after the Olympiad, allowing him to concentrate fully on the immediate challenges before turning his attention to the world title.The clash in Geneva will be a historic meeting between two 20-year-olds, with Sindarov looking to dethrone the champion and Gukesh seeking to defend the crown he won in 2024.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India’s Smriti Mandhana becomes top run-scorer in women’s cricket
articles.summary: Mandhana overtook former India captain Mithali Raj, who had been the top international scorer with 10,868 runs.
articles.body:
India’s batting superstar Smriti Mandhana has become the leading run-scorer in women’s international cricket after smashing a record-breaking 124 off 64 balls in the Women’s Asia Cup in Dubai.

Mandhana overtook former India captain, Mithali Raj , who had been the top international scorer with 10,868 international runs, during her match-winning innings against Hong Kong on Thursday.

It also sealed India’s place in the semifinals of the T20 tournament.

The 30-year-old also became the leading century-maker in women’s international cricket, with 18 hundreds across formats, overtaking Australia’s Meg Lanning and South Africa’s Laura Wolvaardt, who have 17 each.

“It’s just the start,” the India vice-captain said after the game.

Mandhana, who made her India debut in 2013, became the first Indian woman to score international centuries in ‌all three formats when she registered her maiden T20 international hundred last year.

She has two centuries each in Tests and T20Is and 14 in one-day internationals.

“Until I was batting, I didn’t know what record, because I didn’t know what’s the exact runs,” Mandhana said, according to Indian sports outlet Sportstar.

“A very good day for Indian cricket, I would say,” she added.

She also heaped praise on Mithali Raj as a “legend and a role model”.

Mandhana’s knock featured 14 fours and seven sixes as India piled up 193-5 before bowling out Hong Kong for 56 to secure a 137-run victory.

She said Hong Kong’s disciplined bowling made life difficult early ⁠on.

“They were disciplined in the powerplay, bowled really well and the energy they showed ⁠was something we’ll learn from,” said ⁠Mandhana who dedicated her achievement to her family.

articles.body: Star Indian cricketers Virat Kohli and Rishabh Pant, former India stars Virender Sehwag and Suresh Raina, Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker and International Cricket Council (ICC) chairman Jay Shah extended festive greetings to fans and devotees on the occasion of Krishna Janmashtami on Friday.Kohli, Pant, Sehwag lead cricketers' wishesKohli took to his Instagram story to share his wishes, writing, "Jai Shri Krishna, Happy Janmashtami to everyone."Pant, meanwhile, posted his message on X, writing, "Wishing everyone a blessed Janmashtami."Sehwag also turned to X to share his festive greetings, invoking Lord Krishna and his childhood persona."Haathi Ghoda Paal ki, Jai kanhaiya Laal Ki. Wishing you a Krishna Janmashtami as sweet as makhan and as electric as Kanha’s raas! Hare Krishna," Sehwag wrote.Raina shared an elaborate message, praying for happiness, peace and prosperity on the auspicious occasion."Radhe-Radhe. Heartfelt wishes to all on the birth festival of mischievous Nandlal. May Kanha Ji's grace bring love, peace, happiness, and prosperity to every life. Jai Shri Krishna!" Raina wrote.Manu Bhaker, Jay Shah share festive messagesBhaker reflected on the values associated with Lord Krishna in her Janmashtami message, highlighting his qualities of courage, wisdom, love and his commitment to truth and dharma."Best wishes of Shri Krishna Janmashtami. articles.title: Gavin Newsom fires back at Trump after judge dismisses DOJ lawsuit over trans athletes in girls' sports
articles.summary: The Department of Justice says it will appeal after a federal judge dismissed its Title IX lawsuit against California's transgender sports policy.
articles.body: A federal judge has dismissed a Department of Justice lawsuit against California, allowing state rules that let biological males compete in girls' high school sports to remain in place. Following the ruling, Governor Gavin Newsom's office responded in a statement provided directly to OutKick. "This ruling makes clear that President Trump cannot rewrite Title IX by fiat," a spokesperson for Newsom's office said. "He cannot weaponize the law against the American people, and California will keep fighting his attempts to do so." CALIFORNIA GIRLS’ SPORTS ADVOCATES VOW FIGHT AFTER JUDGE TOSSES TRANS ATHLETE CASE: 'FAR FROM OVER' U.S. District Judge Cynthia Valenzuela never ruled on whether California’s policy violates Title IX or whether biological males should compete in girls’ sports. She tossed the case Monday, finding that federal officials failed to give California clear notice that maintaining the policy could cost the state roughly $44 billion in federal education funding. The ruling leaves California’s policy intact for now, while the Justice Department considers an appeal. "We are disappointed by the Court's order and remain committed to enforcing President Trump's agenda of preventing boys from playing in girls' sports," a spokesperson asserted. The federal suit aimed to use Title IX, the landmark 1972 law created to protect female athletes, to safeguard girls' sports. But under Gov. Gavin Newsom and state athletic officials, California has maintained a 2013 policy allowing males to compete on girls’ teams. Newsom has acknowledged on a podcast that fairness is at the heart of the debate over transgender athletes. The Supreme Court’s recent decision upholding state bans did not create a nationwide mandate, leaving California’s policy in effect. CALIFORNIA TRANS ATHLETE PODIUM CONTROVERSY IGNITES OUTRAGE AMONG POLITICIANS, ACTIVISTS California’s policy drew its fiercest backlash in track and field, where Jurupa Valley High School athlete AB Hernandez won four girls’ state titles across two seasons. Hernandez captured back-to-back high jump and triple jump championships and finished third in the long jump, prompting state officials to issue duplicate medals to the girls pushed down the podium. When Hernandez later joined the girls’ varsity volleyball team, the debate moved from competitive fairness to player safety. At least eight teams forfeited against Jurupa Valley, citing fairness and safety concerns over playing against a male competitor. State officials point to the few trans athletes competing in California. Female athletes and advocates say even one male competitor can displace girls, alter a state championship and affect college or NIL opportunities. articles.title: Ireland’s Katie Taylor eyes fairytale finish to trailblazing boxing career
articles.summary: Unbeaten French challenger Flora Pili stands in the way of Taylor becoming undisputed world champion for a third time.
articles.body:
When Katie Taylor began boxing, she sometimes entered junior contests as “K Taylor”, her hair tucked beneath her headguard so nobody would realise she was a girl.

Now aged 40, she is preparing to bow out from the sport in style in front of 80,000 fans at Dublin’s Croke Park on Saturday.

Unbeaten French challenger Flora Pili stands in the way of Taylor becoming undisputed world champion for a third time, with the Irishwoman’s WBA, IBF and WBO super-lightweight titles on the line, along with the vacant WBC belt.

“I’m not sure if there’s any other country in the world where 80,000 people would turn up for a female athlete,” Taylor said this week.

“I want to put on a performance worthy of everyone’s support over the years. This country has travelled around the world to watch me fight,” she added.

Taylor’s storied career has taken her to some of the biggest venues around the globe.

In 2022, she and Amanda Serrano became the first women to headline a boxing card at New York’s Madison Square Garden.

Taylor has also boxed at Wembley, Cardiff’s Principality Stadium and the homes of the Dallas Cowboys and Boston Celtics.

But she craved a return home and the first boxing show at Croke Park – the home of Irish Gaelic sports – since heavyweight great Muhammad Ali beat Al “Blue” Lewis there in 1972.

Taylor, though, warned she cannot let the celebration surrounding her retirement affect her performance.

“It is too dangerous of a sport to have your body in the ring and your heart outside of it thinking about retirement,” she said.

Taylor was just 15 when she contested Ireland’s first officially sanctioned women’s boxing match in 2001.

As a girl, she wrote to Irish world champion Deirdre Gogarty about her difficulty in finding fights and later campaigned for women’s boxing to be admitted to the Olympics.

When women were finally allowed to compete at the London Games in 2012, she won lightweight gold.

Although she fell short of another medal in Rio four years later, it did not dampen Taylor’s rise to stardom after turning professional in 2016.

She needed just seven fights to secure her first world title and later held all four major belts at lightweight before moving up to super-lightweight and achieving the same feat.

Her professional record stands at 25 wins and one defeat.

A fatal gangland shooting at a Dublin boxing weigh-in in the same year Taylor turned professional a decade ago was followed by a long absence of major professional boxing from Ireland.

When Taylor finally fought in Dublin in May 2023, Chantelle Cameron spoiled the party by handing her the sole loss of her professional career.

Taylor reversed the result six months later to claim Cameron’s super-lightweight belts and has since retained them in two more bouts against Serrano in the United States.

Her impact on the other side of the Atlantic was apparent at Wednesday’s public workout where 10-year-old Clodagh Keating was invited into the ring and reduced to tears at meeting her heroine.

Taylor said seeing boxing gyms now filled with girls was “the best part” of her legacy.

She expects the emotion to land after the punches stop.

“In a few days, I’ll make my last ring walk,” she said.

“I’ll look back on this in a few years and I imagine I’ll be overwhelmed”.

articles.title: Jai Arrow gets emotional farewell 100th NRL appearance for South Sydney Rabbitohs after Motor Neurone Disease diagnosis
articles.summary: Jai Arrow retired from rugby league in May following an MND diagnosis; NRL gave South Sydney Rabbitohs special dispensation to include Arrow in their squad and feature as an extra player for the last two matches of the regular season, allowing him to pass 100 appearances for the club
articles.body:
Special dispensation had been granted by the NRL and Rabbitohs to allow Arrow the opportunity to take to the field for the opening kick-off another two times, with the game against Sydney Roosters marking a century of appearances.

Arrow walked his team out onto the field for the Sydney derby, with 'Stand By Me' playing before 'You'll Never Walk Alone' then rang around the Allianz Stadium.

The 31-year-old forward had made 178 appearances overall in the NRL before his retirement announcement earlier his year, playing at Brisbane Broncos and then Gold Coast Titans ahead of joining the Rabbitohs in 2021.

Arrow, also having featured 12 times for Queensland in State of Origin, fought back tears as he was presented to the crowd, who all stood in applause, many holding up banners of support in his name.

Ahead of kick-off, Arrow waved to the crowd before being embraced by his team-mates and then substituted off, with the Rabbitohs having been allowed an extra player in their squad list and an additional rotation.

Rabbitohs head coach Wayne Bennett offered out his arms to Arrow, who was overcome with emotion and could not hold back his tears before sharing an embrace with his wife Berina Colakovic.

Arrow then watched on as South Sydney thrashed the Roosters 50-20 in their final match of the regular season, earning confirm a home elimination tie in the NRL finals.

"It was pretty emotional like it was last week," South Sydney captain Cameron Murray said about Arrow's reception. "I'm just so happy that everyone's been able to get around him.

"He's been able to feel all the love, with 42,000 here today and all getting around him. I know he really appreciates it and we love to see it. We all love him and happy he was able to notch up 100 games."

articles.standfirst: La jugadora de 40 años cayó eliminada en cuartos de final junto a Aranza Osoro ante Gemma Triay y Delfina Brea
articles.summary: La jugadora de 40 años cayó eliminada en cuartos de final junto a Aranza Osoro ante Gemma Triay y Delfina Brea
articles.body: Alejandra Salazar ya es historia viva de Madrid. La jugadora de pádel más laureada de siempre se despidió del Comunidad de Madrid Premier Padel P1, el último torneo de su vida en casa, cayendo con honores en cuartos de final ante las números 1 del mundo: Gemma Triay y Delfina Brea. La madrileña de 40 años, que cuelga la pala a final de temporada tras 26 cursos consecutivos en la máxima élite, se despidió de la prueba que alberga esta semana el Movistar Arena de la capital al lado de Aranza Osoro en el tercer turno de la mañana. Un partido que acabó 6-3 y 6-3 en poco más de una hora pero que tuvo un subidón de emoción tras la última bola. Ahí, el respetable se volcó de lleno con una auténtica leyenda de este deporte, que se dejó llevar por la emotividad del momento y rompió a llorar en otra despedida a una ciudad especial, quizás la que más, cuando ya cuenta los días del calendario para dejarlo definitivamente. Durante más dos décadas Alejandra Salazar no solo ha sido testigo de la transformación del pádel, sino también una de sus grandes protagonistas. Su trayectoria habla por sí sola: 62 títulos oficiales, siete campeonatos del mundo —2010, 2014, 2016, 2018, 2021, 2022 y 2024— y cuatro temporadas al frente del ranking mundial, en 2009, 2016, 2021 y 2022 con tres compañeras distintas. Pero el legado de la madrileña, que recibirá un homenaje especial de Premier Padel entre las finales del domingo, va mucho más allá de los trofeos. Salazar se ha convertido en un referente para miles de niñas que encontraron en ella un modelo a seguir y en una figura clave para entender la evolución del pádel femenino. Generaciones de jugadoras han crecido viéndola competir, compartir pista y marcar el camino en el circuito profesional. En lo que al torneo compete, Brea y Triay accedieron a unas nuevas semifinales en las que se cruzarán con Ariana Sánchez y Andrea Ustero. La pareja 3 del ránking tuvo que emplearse a fondo ante Claudia Jensen y Tamara Icardo para remontar el 7-6 inicial con el 1-6 y 3-6 definitivo en dos horas.

articles.title: Keyaa Banerji lifted 140kg and went viral. Then came thousands of AI images, fake accounts and online abuse — why she created a new Instagram account
articles.summary: More sports News: Indian powerlifter Keyaa Kunal Banerji's remarkable 140kg deadlift was supposed to be a moment of sporting celebration. Instead, the viral attention s.
articles.body: Indian powerlifter Keyaa Kunal Banerji's remarkable 140kg deadlift was supposed to be a moment of sporting celebration. Instead, the viral attention surrounding her silver-medal-winning performance at the 2026 IPF World Sub-Junior & Junior Classic Powerlifting Championships has exposed her to a deeply disturbing side of online fame.The 21-year-old powerlifter has revealed that she has faced sexual harassment, impersonation, conversations about her ethnicity, ancestry and caste, and what she described as thousands of AI-generated images using manipulated versions of her face and body.Banerji opened up about the experience through a series of Instagram stories, explaining why she had created a new account after her previous private profile was suspended. Her decision, she made clear, was not an attempt to chase followers or turn herself into a social media personality, but rather to reclaim control over her own identity and sporting story."I recently won a deadlift silver medal at IPF Jr Worlds for India and while I appreciate the support and recognition, as an Indian female athlete I've also had to deal with sexual harassment online, accounts impersonating me and disturbing conversations surrounding my ethnicity, ancestry and caste?"But it was the scale and nature of the AI manipulation that appeared to trouble her most."And the Worst thousands of Al generated images of me with pictures of my body and face morphed and edited in very disturbing ways it's quite unnerving to be waking up everyday to my feed (and the feeds of every single person I know) flooded with these fake Al pictures," Banerji wrote.From a 140kg celebration to an unwanted online spotlightBanerji competed in the Junior Women's 47kg category at the championships in Sun City, South Africa. Her 140kg deadlift earned her a silver medal in the individual event, behind France's Ines Herbaux, who lifted 165kg. Ireland's Blathnaid O'Dwyer also lifted 140kg.Banerji finished fifth overall in her category after recording a 90kg squat and a 50kg bench press for a 280kg total. Her deadlift was more than three times her competition bodyweight of 45.70kg, helping make the lift an instantly striking clip for social media audiences.The video of the lift spread well beyond the traditional powerlifting community, with users celebrating the young Indian athlete's strength and achievement.But the attention quickly became something Banerji had never sought."I've always been a private person and if you've known me in any capacity/followed my old account you'd know I never posted pictures on it either! It only got more stressful when Instagram suspended my old account (a private account with 300 followers), hence I've made this new one."She said she had initially wanted to keep the new account private too, but felt she had little choice if she wanted to establish which online identity was actually hers."I didn't want to make it public but I'm left with no choice if I want to have a say in a narrative about my own sport and accomplishment and stand up for myself without getting my account suspended again!"The decision effectively put Banerji in the unusual position of becoming more visible online precisely because she wanted to regain control over how she was being portrayed.‘I just want to exist as a girl who likes to deadlift’For Banerji, the sudden fame also sits uneasily with what powerlifting means to her."The purpose of my sport in my life is just to challenge myself in a fun way and I'm grateful to be competing at the level that I am. I never wanted to see myself everywhere like this, in-fact I really despised all these Al posters popping up without my consent. Initially, I just wanted to share this accomplishment with my close friends and family."She stressed that her new account was not created with ambitions of becoming an influencer or monetising the attention generated by her performance."I have no goals of profiting from this account/and no goals of content creation whatsoever, I just want to start fresh with this account and make it clear which one's mine so that Instagram doesn't take my voice away again!"Instead, she wants people who are genuinely interested in her sporting journey to follow the account she controls and avoid amplifying fake versions of her."Thanks for reading it would be really helpful if you could all follow this account if you're interested and redirect people looking for my account to this page because I'd much rather share real pictures of myself and my experience than have you guys look at these Al edits"The sudden transition from being a private social media user to having a public profile has understandably made her uncomfortable."It still makes me uneasy to have a public account all of a sudden as someone who barely uses any social media, but I'd rather take shaky steps towards standing up for myself and having some kind of say in a story about me than reading different versions of it everyday."Banerji also made it clear that she remains willing to talk about the World Championships and her experience in South Africa, but asked people to approach her content with greater sensitivity."If you're curious to know more about Worlds and my experience-I'll be happy to share, let's please do it in a way that's mindful of my mental health!"‘A girl who likes to deadlift’, not an online imageThe powerlifter's posts repeatedly returned to one central point: she wants her sporting identity to remain hers."I truly want the opposite of more publicity over this and I couldn't care less about follower counts etc, I just want a space where I can exist as a girl who likes to deadlift and not an image that's been pulled apart over and over again that feels so inauthentic to me"That distinction is at the heart of Banerji's experience. The 140kg deadlift gave her a moment she could rightly celebrate, but the viral response transformed her sporting accomplishment into a source of unwanted scrutiny.She later acknowledged how much the attention had begun to affect her ability to enjoy what should have been one of the biggest achievements of her young career."a lot of the attention has been overwhelming and in ways I've let it overpower the joy and whimsy that comes with a big win!"Her 140kg lift was not an isolated breakthrough. Banerji's numbers had been steadily improving, with a 127.5kg deadlift at the 2025 national championship and 140kg at the 2026 national championship before matching that figure on the world stage.Her South African performance therefore represented another step in an emerging powerlifting career. Yet the viral nature of the lift brought a different kind of challenge — one she had not trained for and did not ask for.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: SAI creates ‘Little Japan’ in India: Athletes get a taste of Asian Games life in containers
articles.summary: More sports News: BENGALURU: Shipping containers with exteriors painted with cherry blossoms and chochins — traditional Japanese lanterns -- hung on the sides have been.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Shipping containers with exteriors painted with cherry blossoms and chochins — traditional Japanese lanterns -- hung on the sides have been transformed into two-bedroom accommodation. Inside are modern amenities, an LED screen displaying information about the Asian Games and Japanese books such as Ikigai and Kaizen. The menu features ramen, an assortment of sushi, tempura and yakitori.This could easily be Japan. It isn’t, yet.It is the Sports Authority of India (SAI) South Centre in Bengaluru.To help Asian Games-bound athletes acclimatise to the culture, living conditions, and food they will encounter in Japan, SAI has created a slice of the country at its South Centre and the facility in Patiala. Athletes from several disciplines have already utilised the facilities, with team-sport athletes expected to be accommodated in the containers.The containers, built at a cost of around Rs 20 lakh, resulted from an idea conceived earlier this year.“We planned to do this in January, but due to various factors, we could not get them ready. The containers have been operational for a week now, and the volleyball team were one of the first to experience it,” Vishnu Sudhakaran, regional director of the SAI South Centre, told TOI.Each container can accommodate four athletes and was completed in 45 days. Besides overnight stays, the facility has also been used during the day by track and field athletes and the women’s hockey team.And this is not a temporary arrangement. The structure has been designed for permanent use.“Our athletes spend a lot of time away from home and often more than two family members visit them for short durations. We will use this facility as a transit accommodation for visiting families of athletes,” Sudhakaran said.TASTE OF JAPANThe effort to recreate a Japanese experience has extended to the cafeteria.While continental food was introduced last year to help athletes travelling to Europe acclimatise to the cuisine, Japanese dishes were gradually added to the menu from January this year.Chefs at the SAI Centre underwent specialised training in Japanese cuisine under chef Vaibhav Soni of Snowy Foods.“First, the athletes and the chefs were introduced to Japanese culture, such as what and why they eat a particular kind of food, the ingredients they use and what they prefer during breakfast, lunch and dinner,” Soni explained.“The chefs were then taken through the theoretical process followed by the practical knowledge of it. They were then trained in the preparation of various kinds of ramen, sushi, robatayaki, tempura, etc,” he added.Soni has been making regular visits to the centre to oversee the process and ensure the cuisine is prepared as intended.For Indian women’s hockey team striker Lalremsiami, the experience has offered athletes more than just a taste of Japan. “Some of us are used to eating sushi, but for a lot of the athletes it was their first taste of Japanese food. Since we have been experiencing the cuisine for a while now, we know what ingredients go into a particular dish and what to expect on our plate. The containers have given us an experience of what to expect in terms of accommodation,” said the youngster.The idea, according to Sudhakaran, is simple – make Japan feel a little less foreign before the athletes get there.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why Ohio State freshman Jay Timmons may start vs Ball State
articles.summary: Freshman Jay Timmons is in the position to line up at starting nickel back vs Ball State after making an impression at OSU's preseason camp.
articles.body:
Ohio State coach Ryan Day has yet to confirm the defensive starters for the Ball State game , but if Jay Timmons gets the nod at nickel back, he'll become the first OSU freshman to start on defense in a season opener since 2021.

"He's super competitive," Day said. "He's edgy. He just has a knack for the game, and he's got really good instincts."

The Buckeyes entered preseason camp with open spots in the secondary, including the starting nickel back role after Lorenzo Styles Jr. exhausted his eligibility and was selected in the fifth round of the NFL draft by the New Orleans Saints.

Returning senior Jermaine Mathews Jr. took snaps at nickel back during the spring game , but when camp began on Aug. 6, Timmons lined up there for the majority of first-team reps. He impressed teammates with his coverage and recorded a sack during an 11-on-11 period, as Mathews moved back to cornerback.

Timmons lost his black stripe after the sixth day of preseason camp and has kept himself in contention to start in the season opener across the last three weeks of practice.

"He's done a lot to impress everybody," Ohio State sophomore cornerback Devin Sanchez said. "Not just us, but also the offensive coaches too. He's tough out there. ... He's physical, just going out there and touching the ball, making plays on the ball. As a freshman, that's what you've got to do to be felt."

Timmons joined the Buckeyes as their third-highest rated recruit from the Class of 2026 , ranked 25th overall by 247Sports out of Pine-Richland High School in Gibsonia, Pennsylvania.

See Ohio State football in action on Day 3 of training camp

The son of former Pittsburgh Steelers Pro Bowl linebacker Lawrence Timmons, Jay Timmons was originally committed to Florida State before flipping his decision to Ohio State in November. The 5-foot-11, 191 lbs. cornerback arrived in Columbus confident he'd make a push to join the starting lineup.

"I knew when I was his host on his recruitment that he was going to come here and make a difference," Sanchez said. "He told me when he was recruited, 'Hey Dev, I'm going to start at Ohio State my freshman year.'"

The last time an Ohio State freshman started on defense in a season opener was Denzel Burke at cornerback against Minnesota in 2021. Burke is the only freshman defender under Day whose first appearance was as a starter.

With the Buckeyes losing 10 starters from last year, Day predicts the freshman class to have several players who will make an impact early in the season.

"The guys that deserve to have that opportunity through what they've done in terms of earning trust with their teammates, with their coaches ... are going to do that," Day said. "We'll watch their performance on the field and see if they earn more reps."

articles.title: Development never sleeps: Meet the new version of Tigers' Beau Brieske
articles.summary: Weird to say about a guy with 123 games under his belt including six in the postseason, but this month is a kind of audition for Beau Brieske.
articles.body:
CLEVELAND — When you hear talk about player development, you automatically think it's about the younger players, prospects rising through the system, rookies trying to get acclimated to the big leagues.

But development has no age limit, it never stops. And Tigers reliever Beau Brieske is living proof.

Brieske is 28 and has played in parts of five seasons with the Tigers. He's had to reinvent himself a couple times. First, he transitioned from starter to reliever. Then he had to adjust his arsenal again after battling nerve issues in his arm. Now comes another stage of evolution.

He's come back to the Tigers this month with a new weapon. He's brought back a curveball from his stint at Triple-A Toledo, something he abandoned when he transitioned to reliever.

"I wanted something that moves straight down to try to help out with the fastball," he said.

Brieske recently has relied on his power four-seam fastball with changeups that move away from left-handed hitters and sliders that move away from right-handed hitters. Everything he threw was moving east to west.

"Those can be good pitches," he said. "But I think if I'm only doing that, it allows for guys to maybe zone things a little easier. Like, if they pick one (either the fastball or the secondary), they can fight the other off. That's what I was seeing."

Brieske at times struggled to put hitters away for that reason and at-bats would grow long. His strikeout rate in 2024, when he was at peak performance and pitching in leverage situations down the stretch and into the playoffs, was 9.2 per nine innings. It was 6.5 in 2025 and 7.6 in a short sample this year.

"I thought if I could get something that goes down, it would give the hitter another thought, another visual, they have to cover," Brieske said. "Hopefully, in my mind, they would have four different shapes to deal with."

The second benefit to the curveball, it gives Brieske more of an off-speed pitch in his arsenal. His changeup and slider both average around 89 mph. He wants the curveball is spin up there at 85 mph.

"Just having that fourth speed," he said. "It's something I can use to play the front to back game, as well."

The front-to-back game means mixing velocities to get hitters either late on heaters or out in front of the spin and off-speed.

Brieske last thew a curveball in 2022 and it was a 78-mph beauty. Hitters were 3-for-19 against it that year. His changeup was also a slow pitch, 82 mph, with good fading action. What he wouldn't give.

"Yeah, prior to the arm injuries," he said. "It was a really slow, pronated changeup. But the nerve stuff threw a wrench into my ability to throw that. I haven't been able to get the speed differential since. But, like, I can't dwell on it. Let's just adjust."

He is using a slightly modified version of the grip he used for the curveball in 2022.

"I started with the old grip," he said. "But, typical pitch development, I was like, 'Ah, I don't love it,' and you try things, different thumb positions and stuff. I arrived at a slightly adjusted grip from the original, but with the same seam orientation."

He threw the curveball seven times against the Twins on Sept. 1, six of them to right-handed hitters. Probably because of adrenaline, he was throwing it a little firmer than he wants (86.6 mph).

None were put in play and he got one whiff on two swings.

"I just have to be smart about it," he said. "When you start throwing a different pitch, you have to properly ramp it up. You get a new pitch you want to throw it a lot and, all of a sudden, it's like, wow, this (forearm) feels a little tight."

This is a big month for Brieske. Not that he's thinking about it in these terms. His goal is to show the best version of himself and help the Tigers win games. But the reality is, he is in his second year of arbitration. And as such, he is vulnerable to being non-tendered.

Weird to say about a guy with 123 games under his belt including six in the postseason, but this next stretch is almost an audition for Brieske.

➤ LHP Framber Valdez (8-10, 4.36), Tigers: Guardians hitters, in two previous starts against Valdez, worked nine walks. They make him come into the zone and they have done damage when he has (eight runs in 10.2 innings). Valdez is coming off a strong start against the Dodgers in which he established his sinker early and got eight groundball outs in what ended up being a quality start, albeit in a 6-1 loss.

➤ LHP Parker Messick (11-8, 2.46), Guardians: The Tigers didn't do much against him at Comerica Park on Aug. 13, two runs and three hits, but just enough to beat him. They forced him to throw 102 in 5.2 innings with Eduardo Valencia ending his day with a homer. Messick hasn't allowed more than a run in his last three starts, though. He's a fastball bully. His 94-mph four-seamer has a plus-26 run value (Statcast), holding hitters to a .159 average, .250 slugging with a 32.7% strikeout rate.

articles.title: 6-foot-4 Angel Reese towered over by 7-foot-4 Ziyu Zhang in stunning side-by-side
articles.summary: Angel Reese and all of Team USA were busy trying to guard seven-foot-four center Ziyu Zhang during their clash against China in the World Cup.
articles.body:
Angel Reese met her match on the defensive side of the ball while guarding Ziyu Zhang during Team USA's clash with China in their group opener of the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup on Friday morning.

Reese is taking part in her first FIBA World Cup of her national team career. She stands out as a key player on a star-studded roster featuring herself, Caitlin Clark, Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier, and Paige Bueckers among several others.

The U.S. did not have much trouble against China, coasting to a 94-61 blowout win to begin group play. That didn't mean there were no bright spots for the Chinese side. Take in part Zhang, who used her immense height advantage over everyone on Team USA. Reese was no exception as she had trouble keeping the seven-foot-four center in check. There was a clear height different of one foot between Reese and Zhang.

How Angel Reese, USA played against China

Angel Reese and Team USA had a long day guarding Ziyu Zhang. Despite that, they were dominant to begin their 2026 World Cup journey with a blowout victory.

The U.S. controlled the game from start to finish. They jumped out to a 27-14 lead after the first quarter, outmatching their opponents on both sides of the ball. China was unable to catch up as the Americans kept generating offense throughout the course of the game.

Four players scored in double-digits for the U.S. in the victory. Caitlin Clark led the team with 14 points and 11 assists, Paige Bueckers came next with 14 points and four assists, Rhyne Howard scored 14 points, while Jackie Young provided 12 points and three assists.

articles.title: Foxes' Stolarczyk out for season with knee injury
articles.summary: Leicester City goalkeeper Jakub Stolarczyk is ruled out for the rest of the season because of a knee injury.
articles.body:
Leicester City goalkeeper Jakub Stolarczyk has been ruled out for the season with a knee injury.

The 25-year-old sustained the anterior cruciate ligament injury in a collision in the first minute of the Foxes' victory against Plymouth Argyle on Tuesday.

Stolarczyk, a Foxes academy product who established himself as Leicester's first-choice keeper last season, could have surgery as early as next week.

Leicester boss Russell Martin said he is "gutted and hurt" for Stolarczyk.

"I feel so disappointed for the big guy because he has been amazing," Martin told BBC Radio Leicester.

Stolarczyk is the second Leicester player to be ruled out with an ACL injury in the early weeks of the season, with Ben Nelson already having surgery.

Martin said the "only silver lining" about the double injury blow is that the two players will work on their recovery together.

"They are two amazing people, young men that I absolutely love to bits as people and football players and both will be a huge loss on the pitch," Martin said.

"So off it, they will work hard, push each other and drive each other on and I hope we get one or both back before the end of the season.

"But, as it stands, we have to probably prepare for them not to be involved this season."

articles.title: FAU at Florida: Five things to watch in Gators' season opener
articles.summary: Florida kicks off the 2026 season against FAU at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. Here's what to watch for in the first game of the Jon Sumrall era.
articles.body:
A new chapter begins for Florida football and first-year head coach Jon Sumrall as the Gators take on Florida Atlantic Saturday. Florida's offseason was filled with turnover. The program welcomed two new coordinators, 50 roster additions and a new identity under Sumrall and his staff.

Many of the spring headlines around Florida centered on the culture Sumrall plans to establish at UF. Both players and recruits have raved about the team's direction. The opener should provide an early look at how quickly Sumrall has reshaped the program.

Florida is expected to handle the Owls, but Week 1 is about more than the final score. Here are five things to watch as the Gators kick off the 2026 season.

The Georgia Tech transfer makes his first start for the Gators after beating out redshirt freshman Tramell Jones Jr. Philo's command of Buster Faulkner's offense, along with his accuracy, ultimately separated him during fall camp. Can he now use Weeks 1 and 2 to slam the door on any controversy?

Baugh enters 2026 as the clear centerpiece of Florida's offense after rushing for over 1,000 yards in 2025. The junior's success will depend heavily on a retooled offensive line that lost two longtime starters to the NFL in April. Can this unit consistently create running lanes for the preseason First-Team All-American?

The Gators' secondary gets an immediate test against Veltkamp, who helped FAU lead the nation with 340.2 passing yards per game last season. While he threw for more than 3,600 yards last year, he also tossed 17 interceptions. It would be encouraging to see the group grab a few picks on Saturday. Reinforcements from the transfer portal add experience at safety with senior DJ Coleman from Baylor and at nickelback with Kanye Clark from UCLA, joining senior strong safety Bryce Thornton.

Saturday represents the first real look at what Sumrall's version of Florida football will evolve into. I will be keeping a close eye on the overall demeanor of the team as well as Sumrall's presence on the sideline. I expect to see more discipline and cleaner execution under this new regime. Most importantly, how the Gators respond to any early adversity will be key to affirming this new identity.

5. Impact underclassmen (Wilson, Hanks III)

Florida will lean on a few young players as key contributors on Saturday. Redshirt freshman receiver Dallas Wilson and cornerback Ben Hanks III have been impressive during camp and are both listed as starters. Both former blue-chip prospects have SEC-level talent and athleticism — it will be interesting to see how quickly they can translate their potential into production.

articles.title: Why Man United did not sign Nicolas Tagliafico after considering “secret deal” before deadline
articles.summary: 2Manchester United’s pursuit of a new left-back ultimately ended in disappointment this summer. The Red Devils spent much of the transfer window focusing on...
articles.body:
Manchester United's pursuit of a new left-back ultimately ended in disappointment this summer. The Red Devils spent much of the transfer window focusing on midfield reinforcements, signing Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, and Carlos Baleba .

The left-back position was also a priority for the English giants this summer, especially with Luke Shaw already on the wrong side of 30. The veteran full-back's contract expires at the end of this season, further complicating matters for INEOS.

While the Englishman started every Premier League game last season, it was imperative to lay down succession plans for the future. Several emerging and established candidates were monitored for the role, including Newcastle United's Lewis Hall , Barcelona's Alejandro Balde, and RB Leipzig's David Raum.

Unfortunately, United failed to land any of their left-back targets and ended the summer without adding cover for Shaw to their squad. Acclaimed journalist Fabrizio Romano has now named a surprise candidate who was also eyed as an option for the job.

Speaking on the Here We Go podcast, Romano said that United considered Nicolas Tagliafico in the closing days of the summer transfer window but ultimately opted against the move. He said: "One secret deal that nobody knows about?"

"I can tell you that, for example, one of the players Manchester United considered at left back, because we know they were looking at left back, was also Nicolas Tagliafico."

"Man United had Nicolas Tagliafico around the final days of the window as a possibility. Then they decided not to proceed for several reasons."

"So it was an internal decision by United, it was not the player deciding or anyone else. So it was under consideration. Let's say like this, alongside other names, Ian Maatsen and Alejandro Balde."

United already have an experienced left-back in Luke Shaw, who is on the wrong side of 30, so it is understandable why a move for Tagliafico failed to materialise. However, the Argentine did make a good case for himself at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, where he was assured at the left-back position.

The 34 year old started five of La Albiceleste's eight games in the tournament, including the final, which they lost 1-0 to Spain after extra time. Tagliafico is highly experienced at club level, having also played under former United manager Erik ten Hag at Ajax.

Last season, the Argentine registered three assists in 30 appearances across competitions for Lyon.

Nicolas Tagliafico Stats: 2025/26 Season

Tagliafico has entered the final year of his contract with the Ligue 1 giants and would have represented an affordable option for United. However, INEOS cannot be blamed for ultimately abandoning the pursuit.

United have taken a gamble by not signing a new left-back this summer, and could be left to rue that decision as the season unfolds. However, it could also be a chance for a younger star like Harry Amass to seize the opportunity with both hands.

articles.title: Bone Valley opens soon at Streamsong in Florida
articles.summary: Architect David McLay Kidd gives players plenty of room, but birdies won't always come easy.
articles.body:
Several of architect David McLay Kidd's most popular courses have focused on extreme and creative playability , with Gamble Sands in Washington and Mammoth Dunes at Sand Valley in Wisconsin as prime examples. Even his first-ever design, the original Bandon Dunes layout at the famed resort of the same name in Oregon, put playability at the forefront.

Kidd had a few deviations from the playability theme in his career, but in recent years he has talked at length about designing courses that are approachable for any level of golfer. The trick, he has said, is to challenge the best players while allowing less-skilled golfers to keep swinging.

Consider that challenge accepted at Bone Valley in Florida, his latest completed creation that will open in late September for preview play at the well-regarded Streamsong Resort. Built with an appreciation of the resort's other courses and with those layouts' DNA in mind, Kidd has constructed a new, full-sized 18 that offers ample width and plenty of opportunities to bounce balls into greens – those are keys to playability for less-skilled players.

But just as megalodon shark teeth can be found in the sand piles left over from the site's history as a phosphate mining operation, Bone Valley can offer a bit of a bite. Stray too far from the best scoring lines, and even the best players will struggle with the angles as they attempt to set up birdie putts.

"My team and I felt like we got to build something really, really fun both visually, strategically, creatively," Kidd said. "I think golfers, when they come here, won't be disappointed. I think they'll have a blast trying to figure out how to navigate their way through. I think every hole has a dozen different attacks you could make, a thousand different ways you could recover from error. It's not overly penal, but she is going to put up a fight against scoring. I think I've been able to refine that over the last dozen years or so."

Bone Valley's full grand opening is slated for January 26. In the meantime, check out our video of the completed course , featuring narration by Kidd.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark makes statement after breaking Team USA FIBA World Cup record
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark didn’t let her record-breaking performance distract from the bigger goal at the FIBA World Cup. Caitlin Clark delivered a historic performance...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark didn't let her record-breaking performance distract from the bigger goal at the FIBA World Cup.

Caitlin Clark delivered a historic performance in her FIBA Women's World Cup debut, leading Team USA to a 94–61 win over China. Coming off the bench, she posted 14 points, 3 rebounds, and a game-high 11 assists with zero turnovers.

Her 11 dimes set a new USA record for the most assists in a World Cup debut, surpassing Alyssa Thomas's previous mark of nine. She also became the first American player to notch a points-assists double-double in a World Cup game since 1994, while setting a USA record for the most assists without a turnover in tournament history.

Speaking in the FIBA postgame press conference, Caitlin Clark credited her teammates for allowing her to even get 11 assists in the first place.

She said: "You know, obviously playing around so many talented players. Obviously our guards are incredible, and our post players too. But anybody I pass the ball to it feels like they're never going to miss a shot. So that's one of my goals when I come into the game, facilitate, play fast, set up my teammates, get into the paint, get some penetration. Especially with their zone, that was one of my focus points."

It speaks volumes of the person that Caitlin Clark is to divert the attention onto her teammates after breaking a couple of records on her FIBA World Cup debut.

articles.title: Naomi Osaka rips US Open influencers causing match disruptions
articles.summary: Naomi Osaka had her first round match at the US Open interrupted by influencers in the crowd. The tournament has seen an influx of influencers this year and...
articles.body:
Naomi Osaka had her first round match at the US Open interrupted by influencers in the crowd. The tournament has seen an influx of influencers this year and the reaction has not been mixed as people just seem generally annoyed by their disruptions .

Osaka was asked about the influencers during a press conference following her round two victory. She noted that the umpire had "told everyone to be quiet more than I've ever heard an umpire tell a crowd to be quiet." And in her first round match she mostly ignored the noise, but there was a moment when people were shouting.

Osaka was diplomatic, pointing out that they could help grow the game, but wished they better followed the etiquette of the sport.

"I think obviously if you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport," Osaka said. "And I feel like it's common courtesy to read up on the sport, especially the etiquette. I feel like it could be a good thing for people to make the sport of tennis popular to their specific audience, but I think it has to be managed a lot better, especially in the situation like my first-round match. Overall, I think there are huge positives. I'm not the one to… you want people to continue to grow the sport."

Osaka herself has been very influencer-y during the tournament. She showed up to her first round match in a look inspired by Allen Iverson and took a page out of LeBron James' fashion playbook in round two. Her next match will be against Elise Mertens on Saturday. As usual, all eyes will be on Osaka. If the influencers don't cause another distraction.

articles.title: Baggies transfer window 'laser-focused'
articles.summary: Fan writer Chris Hall reflects on West Bromwich Albion's summer transfer window.
articles.body:
The old saying tells us that patience is a virtue but, unfortunately, it's something that is often in short supply in football.

There's often very little time or thought given to building something long-term, especially if doing so could come at the expense of immediate success.

However, Albion have bucked that trend this summer.

The Throstles signed nine senior outfield players during the transfer window.

Of those nine, seven were 23 or younger, five were signed from outside the UK, and seven had not played in the Championship before.

Albion's ownership did exactly what they said they would do.

In an open letter to fans on 26 June, chairman Shilen Patel said, "We aim to build a squad of dynamic, hard-working, and well-coached players with an emphasis on talent we believe will grow in their time with us.

"When we look at our most successful recruitment, there are clear commonalities and they have nothing to do with how much we spent to bring the player here."

The Baggies could have approached the window in a similar manner to many of their competitors, paying inflated prices for proven Championship talents.

Wrexham were accused by Sheffield United boss Chris Wilder last week of "blanket bombing", Albion's approach was the antithesis of that, remaining laser-focused and refusing to deviate.

That meant that if the right deal didn't come up, Albion didn't compromise.

This meant that the Baggies didn't fill certain positions in the squad they perhaps would have liked to, but the players that did come in were largely young and exciting.

However, with so much youth and so many players recruited from abroad, there is a need for patience.

Albion started the season superbly with two wins from two.

But, with one point from the past two games, there have been calls for more of the new players to be blooded.

The scintillating early season form of new boy Jimmy-Jay Morgan probably raised expectations that the other new signings could do the same, and Rabby Nzingoula's thrilling second half showing on Wednesday night will have furthered that feeling.

Others, however, may need a softer launch

Kareem Tunde excited at Middlesbrough off the bench but struggled a little in a first start on Wednesday, while Albion's new striker Barney Stewart is clearly being eased into Championship life with just 21 minutes in the league so far.

The Scotland U21 international has enjoyed an incredible rise since leaving university football in 2024, but this is the biggest leap he's made to date, and he will probably need time to adapt

Felix Horn Myhre and Nolan Galves are the two who have been thrown straight into the starting XI, but both inclusions were somewhat enforced.

Galves was the only senior right-back option prior to the deadline day signing of Brayann Pereira, while Myhre was given an opening day start due to the sale of Alex Mowatt 48 hours prior, and then continued due to the subsequent suspension and illness of Aune Heggebo.

You would imagine that Morrison would, ideally, have liked two players new to the division to have had a more gradual introduction to it.

Albion's entire strategy over the summer was to sign players with a view to the future, but the consequence of this is that we are likely to see the best of our new assets in time.

After being the oldest squad in the league a mere three-years ago, Bilkul have done an incredible job of turning Albion into a team awash with young, hungry players in a handful of windows.

I believe that hard work will pay off, but we might have to be a bit patient before we truly reap the benefits.

articles.title: Carlson Gets the Call: Have the Saints found their solution at kicker?
articles.summary: The All-Pro brings some experience and hopefully some consistency to the Saints kicking game
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints appear to have found their answer at kicker with veteran Daniel Carlson, a two-time All-Pro who brings a proven track record and a powerful leg to New Orleans' special teams unit.

The former Las Vegas Raiders kicker signed with New Orleans on Aug. 24 and wasted little time making his case for the Saints' kicking job. Carlson took part in his first practice just two days later and then suited up for the Saints' preseason matchup against Dallas two days after that. He converted both of his field-goal attempts, including a game-winning 53-yarder, in the Saints' 27-24 victory over the Cowboys.

Carlson's quick transition helped him move ahead of Charlie Smyth and Tanner Brown, who had been competing for the job since Brown joined the Saints in June.

Saints head coach Kellen Moore praised Carlson's performance despite having just a brief window to evaluate him, while acknowledging the difficult decision the team faced at kicker.

"We really only had two days with Daniel, and so obviously feel like he showed himself well," Moore said. "Made a nice kick at Dallas. More time on task will be beneficial for him. Those are tough decisions — Tanner is a kicker in this league, Charlie is a kicker in this league, I think we had some really good guys there. Daniel is going to do a great job for us."

After spending his previous eight seasons with the Raiders, Carlson made 225 of 259 career field-goal attempts (86.9%) and earned first-team All-Pro honors in 2022. He will now take over the kicking duties in New Orleans, hoping to provide stability at a position that has been inconsistent for the Saints over the past few seasons.

articles.title: Gabriel Martinelli omits Mikel Arteta in Arsenal farewell post after 'uncomfortable' move
articles.summary: Gabriel Martinelli has completed a $81.2 million move to Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal, omitting manager Mikel Arteta from his farewell message after seven...
articles.body:
Gabriel Martinelli pointedly excluded Mikel Arteta from his farewell message with Arsenal in an icy manner, having signed for Al-Hilal in a £60 million ($81.2 million) transfer on Thursday.

The 25-year-old found himself considered expendable at the Emirates Stadium this summer, with Christos Tzolis and Ebere Eze assuming prominence in Arteta's starting XI.

Consequently, Martinelli was connected with numerous clubs in Turkey and Saudi Arabia before ultimately deciding on Pro League powerhouse Al-Hilal.

The Brazilian traveled to the Middle East earlier this week for a medical examination, before he was presented by Al-Hilal on Thursday - with Arsenal also posting a message of gratitude for the left-winger's contributions since 2019.

The club stated, as per football.london : "Forever a Gunner. The club can confirm that Gabriel Martinelli has joined Al-Hilal on a permanent deal. Thank you for everything and best of luck, Gabi."

Martinelli also utilized social media to post a sincere tribute of his own to the club, though, without even acknowledging Arteta after their relationship apparently deteriorated.

He stated: "I can only thank the staff and my teammates. Thank you to the chefs, kit staff, doctors, doormen, security staff, media team, cleaning staff, physios, and every single teammate who has been part of my story from 2019 until today. Thank you to everyone who helped me grow during this journey.

"And to the fans, thank you for everything. Since my first day, you made me feel at home. Every time I stepped on the pitch, despite everything, I tried to give everything I had for this shirt. To Arsenal, thank you for believing in me and giving me the chance to show myself to the world.

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

"Most of all, I want to thank my family and my wife, who have been by my side throughout this entire journey, giving me all the emotional support I needed to overcome the challenges that only we truly know. It has been a long journey, too much history and now it has come to an end.

"I'm writing this with tears in my eyes, so hard to put 7 years into words. From 35 to 11. Once a Gunner, Always a Gunner. Goodbye, and thank you again."

The heartfelt farewell follows Ian Wright's scathing criticism of the club's behind-the-scenes handling of Martinelli's exit, with the Arsenal legend expressing how "uncomfortable" his former club's conduct made him feel.

Addressing the situation after Arsenal's season-opening victory over Coventry City, Wright told Sky Sports: "With respect to Martinelli and the way he's being treated at the moment, it really makes me uncomfortable.

"He always gives 100 percent, we're not saying he's the greatest, but he's come up with some big moments for Arsenal in big games, and the way he's being treated at the end here – I know they might want him out and there's a lot of guys saying it's time for him to move on, but there's ways of doing that should suit him as well."

Asked what he meant by the treatment, Wright explained: "Not being in the squad tonight, not being spoken to, doesn't know what's going on."

He continued: "Yes, I do know this, I know this. Not being involved in the Community Shield squad, not being involved tonight, he doesn't know what's happening, he's got a year left.

"If you bring Vini in, that kind of level, Martinelli can say to himself, 'Well okay they've brought him in and Tzolis, I might be third. ' But if you're bringing in Tzolis and Madueke's there, you're thinking to yourself, 'I've got something to offer here.'

"So for him to be nowhere near it, just makes me feel a bit sad for him. I think he's done enough in this squad to be treated with a bit more respect than he's been treated at the moment."
