articles.title: Birmingham relishing Man City challenge on WSL return
articles.summary: Birmingham City head coach Amy Merricks says her side will go "toe-to-toe" with Women's Super League champions Manchester City on their return to the top fli...
articles.body:
Birmingham City head coach Amy Merricks says her side will go "toe-to-toe" with Women's Super League champions Manchester City on their return to the top flight.

Birmingham clinched the WSL 2 title on the final day of last season to secure promotion and end a four-year stint in the second tier, but have been given a tough assignment on the opening day of the 2026-27 campaign.

Merricks' side will travel to the Joie Stadium in Manchester on Sunday (14:30 BST), where a 6-0 defeat in the same fixture in May 2022 condemned them to relegation.

Man City won all 11 of their home WSL matches last season , but Merricks is relishing the challenge awaiting her team.

"I think it's a great time to play Man City. We know it's going to be a challenge but we are well and truly up for it. We are here to compete, not just make up the numbers," Merricks said in her pre-match media conference.

"Our focus is on ourselves, we appreciate and respect who they are and what they have, but our mindset doesn't change."

Last season Birmingham scored an average of 2.09 per game and earned a reputation as an attacking team, something Merricks is not willing to sacrifice just because they will face tougher opposition this term.

"There is a core part of our identity that is non-negotiable for us as Blues and myself as a head coach," she added.

"We are a progressive team, we will find ways to create and score. We are really clear on what our strengths are and what we need to maximise.

"This is the best league in the world, it is going to be tough and a challenge, but what we can't do is lose our strengths. We have to amplify those and put ourselves in the best position possible.

"We have to focus on what we can control and that's how we can compete. We don't fear anyone. I think we showed that in the cup competitions last year."

Man City boss Andree Jeglertz knows that only too well - Sunday's match comes five months to the day since his side were made to work for a 1-0 victory away at Birmingham in the quarter-finals of the Women's FA Cup.

"We had a tough game against them last year. They were tactically very good and destroyed all the space on the field, defending low and their transitioning was very good. There are threats in their team we need to give attention to," Jeglertz said.

"Playing against a team that is new in the league is always a challenge because I know they are coming in with a lot of energy in the first game."

Man City are beginning their first league title defence in a decade, but Jeglertz does not want his side's mentality to change just because they have something to lose.

"We are still chasing, chasing to win again. If you start protecting things, I don't think that will help us. We need to be in a mood of hunger, trying to win again, to compete in different tournaments.

"If we drop a little bit in performance or attitude, teams will go past us."

Jeglertz confirmed that Man City will be without forward Vivianne Miedema until at least late autumn because of a knee injury, while defender Rebecca Knaak will miss the visit of Birmingham with a foot issue.

Defender Jade Rose and midfielder Grace Clinton have returned to training, but summer signing Niamh Charles is "a big question mark" for Sunday.

articles.title: Naomi Osaka Urged Influencers At The US Open To “Read Up” On Tennis Etiquette
articles.summary: "It’s common courtesy to read up on the sport."
articles.body:
The US Open — the final grand slam of the tennis season — is well underway in New York City . And, as you may have heard, there's been a lot of talk about influencers.

As any tennis fan will know, there is a huge amount of etiquette in the sport, for players and spectators alike. If you're watching a tennis match, it is expected that you should not make noise during active play so as not to distract the players.

At most major tournaments, this is not an issue. However, as the US Open has gained popularity in recent years, concerns have been raised about the level of noise during matches.

I, for one, have noticed a huge increase in the number of celebrities and influencers on my timeline who have attended the US Open in the past few years. And according to the BBC , around 100 influencers and content creators have been granted accreditation for this year's tournament, double the number from 2025.

Now, this isn't to say that celebrities and influencers are solely to blame for the disruption issues. However, there have been numerous instances suggesting that some people in the luxury suites are more interested in creating content than actually watching tennis.

Naomi Osaka is one of the most exciting athletes in the tournament. But during her opening-round match at Arthur Ashe Stadium on Monday, the umpire was forced to reprimand a group of influencers who were making noise and capturing content with a portable ring light while Naomi was serving. "Guys, please, in the suite behind me, please thank you guys, please take your seat," the chair umpire could be heard announcing , while Naomi and her opponent, Anastasia Zakharova, were left waiting on the court.

Two videos from the Osaka/Zakharova match are circulating online, one of which shows a woman using a bright ring light while staging a photoshoot during play. Another clip — with over 33 million views on X — shows a group in a luxury suite talking loudly in unison, while a spectator in front of them looks visibly annoyed.

Fortunately for Naomi, she won the match in spite of the distractions; however, that doesn't mean there's not an important conversation to be had.

Speaking in a post-match press conference after her second-round win on Thursday, the four-time Grand Slam champion was asked about the ongoing influencer debate and urged all spectators to respect the sport's "etiquette."

"If you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport," Naomi told reporters. "I feel like it's common courtesy to read up on the sport. Especially the etiquette. I feel like it could be a good thing for people to make the sport of tennis popular to their specific audience. But I think it has to be managed a lot better, especially in the situation like my first round match."

Though there wasn't such a notable disruption in her second-round match, Naomi noted that the general noise in the crowd was still an issue. "Today the umpire told everyone to be quiet more than I've ever heard an umpire tell a crowd to be quiet," she said, clarifying that she finds the noise more annoying than people using bright ring lights. "I tell people I normally just focus on the match and the court, but there was a moment where there was people shouting and you could hear it quite clearly. I think it bothered my opponent, too."

Despite this, Naomi did say she thought there were still "huge positives" regarding the influx of interest from social media stars. "You want people to continue to grow the sport," she said. "I just think it has to be in a way that everyone knows the rules and the etiquette."

Naomi is not the only tennis player to have weighed in on the influencer debate this tournament. US player Jessica Pegula said , "I can appreciate the influencers coming and kind of showcasing the US Open experience. But I do think that it's tough when you see videos like that when they're taking pictures and using the selfie lights. People are down there trying to perform, and it's their career and their job. It seems like a bit disrespectful. I think it's gotten a little maybe too much."

Well, if you're heading to any tennis matches soon, make sure you read the room. You can find Naomi's full press conference here .

articles.title: Moyes disappointed by Everton transfer window but insists club must keep moving forward
articles.summary: David Moyes admits he was disappointed by Everton’s transfer window but insists the club must move on and continue pushing in the right direction ahead of Su...
articles.body:
David Moyes admits he was disappointed by Everton's transfer window but insists the club must move on and continue pushing in the right direction ahead of Sunday's clash with Manchester United.

Everton were unable to complete all of their planned business before the deadline, while losing Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City and Tim Iroegbunam during a late period of activity.

"Disappointed, we didn't do more business," Moyes said. "Disappointed, things didn't go our way in the end.

"But sometimes in football you have to live with disappointments and we will and we'll move on."

The failed pursuit of Folarin Balogun was one of the major setbacks, with Moyes confirming the deal collapsed because of an issue with the striker's medical.

"Ultimately it happens in football," he said. "The player had a problem in his medical and that was simply it. So there's no other stories behind it really, that's exactly what happened."

Everton had also been hoping to generate funds from player departures, with Moyes acknowledging that the decision to retain Harrison Armstrong affected their ability to complete further deals.

"We were looking to get some money in and ultimately those things were getting talked about," he said.

"We lost Illy who was someone we definitely didn't want to lose."

Moyes admitted Everton's small squad will now require players to be versatile, while the door could open for academy prospects.

"We've got a really small squad now and it sometimes gives people opportunities maybe who haven't had them," he said.

"You need to be given that chance to show what you can do."

The Everton boss confirmed the club are also looking at the free-agent market, although he stressed his ambition remains to challenge towards the top end of the Premier League.

"The disappointment would be that I want to keep pressing on, I want to keep the club moving in the right direction and I want the players to believe we're moving in the right direction."

Moyes also addressed reports of a potential late Chelsea bid for James Garner, dismissing them as "completely untrue".

He acknowledged, however, that Everton may eventually have to sell players if major clubs come calling.

"I've had to sell Mikel Arteta to Arsenal and I've had to sell Wayne Rooney to Man United," Moyes said.

"If we're going to lose players we want to keep getting better."

Moyes also revealed he has not discussed potential investment with Everton's new owners, saying it was outside his jurisdiction.

However, he believes the different departments at the club are gradually becoming more aligned.

"I think we've got new owners in who are still finding their way at the club," he said.

"As we get to know each other a lot better and a bit more I think it will get better."

Attention now turns to Sunday's meeting with Manchester United, with Moyes praising Michael Carrick for guiding United back into the Champions League.

"I think he's done an amazing job," Moyes said. "He's steadied them, I think he knows how the club runs, how it works.

articles.title: Why Raiders' second-round WR buried on depth chart in 2025 could be 'X-factor' this year
articles.summary: It might finally be time for this second-round WR to shine.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders are all about figuring out what works on the offensive side of the ball during the 2026 season. It's not meant to be a contending season, but rather one to figure out what they have and what they need.

While Ashton Jeanty, Brock Bowers, and Fernando Mendoza are the future at RB, TE, and QB, the wide receiver room is very much up in the air. Tre Tucker is the No. 1 WR, but after him, the WR room is a lot of unknowns.

But for ESPN's Ben Solak , the "X-Factor" in the Raiders' offense could be second-round WR Jack Bech. After being buried on the depth chart in his rookie season, Bech could become the Raiders' No. 2 WR in 2026 and have a breakout year in the process.

Why Raiders 'X-Factor' is 2nd-round WR Jack Bech

"But if Bech can make big plays as the third wideout on the field, he'll quickly climb the depth chart and give the Raiders the secondary playmakers they desperately need behind Bowers," Solak writes.

The second-year WR hasn't won the No. 2 job in the Raiders' receiver room, as Jalen Nailor is making a case for that job. But it would not be a surprise if Bech eventually won over Klint Kubiak and took over at No. 2 WR.

Solak hinted at how that could happen, noting Bech's propensity to do the "dirty work," and also how he "blocks well and can take easy targets for big gains..."

Being able to do the dirty work of blocking as a receiver and also making nice plays after the catch could help his case to earn more playing time.

If Nailor struggles, or Bech simply shines in his limited role early in the season, as the year rolls along, Bech could wind up as a starter for this team, maybe around the same time that Mendoza ends up as the starter.

Last season, in 16 games but with very limited opportunities on a poor offense, while also being buried on the depth chart for much of the year, Bech caught 20 passes for 224 yards and no touchdowns.

It was a weak season for the No. 58 overall pick in the second round of the 2025 NFL Draft. While last year was a letdown, the 6-foot-1, 214-pound receiver could be in store for a big breakout in 2026.

There is still plenty of uncertainty about Bech's ability, but Solak believes that the second-round WR could be in store for a big season now that the coaching staff is in a better place and the WR2 competition is wide open.

articles.title: Mizzou Football: Death Row Defense Alive and Well in Season Opener
articles.summary: MU’s offense will grab most of the headlines from Thursday’s win. The defense’s first half might be just as important.
articles.body:
Reports of Death Row Defense's decline may have been greatly exaggerated.

Missouri's defense seized control and didn't give it up until the game was well in hand during the Tigers' 54-14 season opening win over Arkansas-Pine Bluff.

"I feel like our defense played to a standard that we chose," linebacker Robert Woodyard Jr. said, "and the mindset that we anticipated going into the game was really to dominate."

The Golden Lions didn't move the chains on offense until the second quarter. They didn't cross midfield until the second half. And they scored their first touchdown of the night with 2:31 left in the third quarter after MU pulled its starters coming out of the half.

That performance should be taken with a few large grains of salt — Arkansas-Pine Bluff went 4-8 in the FCS last year, after all.

But for a unit viewed by many as the team's biggest concern entering the season, Thursday night's performance had plenty of positives to pick from.

The defense allowed just six total yards in the first half, and the Golden Lions had negative (that's right, negative) 26 rushing yards heading into halftime. More often than not, holding the opposition to 0.2 yards per play across 30 minutes of action will get the job done.

Mizzou also did all of the above while recording two tackles for loss — with no sacks or forced turnovers. The defense didn't come up with any major plays, but it still dictated the action for two full quarters when on the field.

"I feel like we executed pretty well," defensive back Elijah Dotson said, "At the end of the day, you always find something to clean up; like coach said, we've got a lot of things to fix. But I feel like we did a good job today."

The night wasn't all positives for defensive coordinator Corey Batoon's unit. The Tigers will need those big plays moving forward, and the defense bent slightly in the second half once the coaches subbed in the reserves.

"We were able to create some constriction in the pocket, but we weren't able to shed blocks. Guys were going to get out and escape," head coach Eli Drinkwitz said, "So we'll have to go back and look at the tape, but there's things we've got to improve on for sure."

The defensive front left Memorial Stadium with room for improvement in the pass rush, but mitigated that impact by effectively serving as a brick wall against the Golden Lions' rushing attack.

"Our guys up front, they set the standard," Dotson said, "We always talk about we've got to win in the trenches, and that's what they did today."

The Tigers' experience on the interior of the defensive line was a difference maker. Defensive tackles Marquis Gracial and Sterling Webb are the unit's only two returning players who more than five starts in 2025, and the positional rotation also features a fifth-year senior in Jalen Marshall.

Veterans weren't the only players that stood out, though. Dotson recorded three tackles, including one for a loss, and also forced a fumble that was recovered by Arkansas-Pine Bluff.

Arguably his biggest play of the night was one that never officially happened. Dotson came up with what would have been MU's first interception of the season, but the play was overturned when Nicholas Rodriguez was flagged for roughing the passer.

"What he did today was really what he did most of the spring," Drinkwitz said of Dotson, "He's a guy that played multiple positions for us, and I felt like he's a great tackler and a guy in space."

After battling with Kensley Louidor-Faustin for the starting spot throughout fall camp, Dotson looks like a player who could become key to a new-look secondary that will rely heavily on production from transfers.

The secondary didn't see any major breakdowns during the opening half — not an easy task for a group learning to play alongside each other and communicate in a game setting for the first time.

"I felt like it was really good. It's something we've been working on in practice every day," Dotson said, "We always talk about communication. That's a key thing; if you can't communicate, you can't win."

Much of the talk following the season opener will focus on Mizzou's offense, and for good reason. Eli Drinkwitz's attack put up 40 points and over 400 yards of total offense in the first half as Austin Simmons looked comfortable and commanding in his Tigers debut.

The defense also showed plenty of promise when its starters were in.

This year's version of Death Row Defense is unlikely to reach the heights of 2025, when the group was a top-10 defense in the nation. But if Batoon can help this unit to a top-25 performance — especially with an offense that looks ready to roll — MU might be able to make some noise in the always-tough SEC.

articles.title: Charlie Woods conjures up a par from the footpath at the Island Green
articles.summary: Charlie Woods made some short-game magic on the TPC Sawgrass Stadium Course's Island Green on Sept. 4 to get into contention at the Junior Players.
articles.body:
PONTE VEDRA BEACH | Charlie Woods made some of his father's short-game magic come to life at the Players Stadium Course at TPC Sawgrass on Sept. 4 during the first round of the American Junior Golf Association Junior Players Championship .

It wasn't "Better than Most" but it was pretty good for a 17-year-old.

Woods, who began the first round at No. 10, was coming off birdies at Nos. 15 and 16 that offset early bogeys at the 11th and 14th holes. Facing a 134-yard tee shot at the 17th hole Island Green, with no wind and a back-right hole placement, Woods pulled his wedge a bit and for a few seconds, thought he had found the water.

But fans standing on a bank behind the hole gave a baseball umpire's "safe" signal, indicating the ball was dry.

It was, but it would be no easy shot. The ball had landed on the footpath players use to enter the green and rolled about 30 feet down. It was on short grass and he had a stance but the ball was tight to the pin, with little room to work with.

Woods then chipped the ball barely onto the putting surface. The ball checked and rolled to within 4 feet. He made the putt for par.

Woods' father Tiger made one of the most famous shots in Players Championship history at No. 17 in the third round in 2001, when he drained a double-breaking, 60-foot putt for birdie. The feat has been dubbed ever since the "Better than Most" putt, since that was what NBC commentator Gary Koch kept saying when the ball was tracking to the hole, referring to most players being unable to get the ball close from that spot.

Tiger Woods went on to win the first of his two Players Championships that year. Charlie Woods is one of four sons of past Players winners to compete in the Junior Players, including Dru Love (Davis Love III), Tyler McCumber (Mark) and Cameron Kuchar (Matt).

Charlie Woods closed out his front nine by draining an 18-foot putt for birdie at the par-4 18th hole. At the time he made the putt, he moved into a tie for second at 1-under par.

Woods will tee off at No. 1 at 10 a.m. in the second round on Sept. 5. The final round is Sept. 6.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers faces brutal QB rankings check while earning unexpected Kyler Murray comparison
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers has received a reality check in the latest quarterback rankings. The Steelers star sits 20th among 93 quarterbacks in FanSided’s pre-season pro...
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers has received a reality check in the latest quarterback rankings. The Steelers star sits 20th among 93 quarterbacks in FanSided's pre-season project.

A panel of 50 experts graded every signal-caller on a 12-point scale. Rodgers scored 7.52, landing him in a tier of his own titled 'Solid Starter'.

It is not the company a future Hall of Famer expects to keep.

With Murray comparison Rodgers ranked 20th as Steelers prep for Week 1

The 42-year-old sits just below a cluster of 11 quarterbacks in the 'Strong QB1' tier, which includes Caleb Williams, Jordan Love, Trevor Lawrence, Jayden Daniels and Jared Goff.

Even more brutal: C.J. Stroud ranks one spot ahead of him, and Kyler Murray sits directly behind at No. 21.

Murray is grouped in the 'Game Manager' category, alongside Daniel Jones, Cam Ward, Jaxson Dart and Bryce Young. Rodgers was less than a tenth of a point from falling into that same bracket.

His numbers last season still had substance, with 3,322 yards, 24 touchdowns and seven interceptions in 16 games. But the panel clearly see the decline in mobility and the hesitation in the pocket.

With Mike McCarthy back on the sideline and the Steelers hosting the Falcons in Week 1, Pittsburgh will hope the reunion sparks a resurgence.

Given his age and where he ranks, grounded expectations are the message for Steelers fans.

The Murray connection is where the story turns unexpected. Former teammate Chris Streveler believes the two quarterbacks share more than people realise, at least in how the media treats them.

'I've been around a lot of guys who have been somewhat misunderstood. Kyler being one of them. Aaron Rodgers was another. I had positive experiences with both of those guys,' Streveler said, per Action Network's Kyle Odegard.

'The media is going to always take those narratives and run with them, try to build them up.'

Streveler also believes Murray's mix of arm and leg talent is elite, putting him in a class with Lamar Jackson.

Rodgers will be watching that comparison from Pittsburgh. One veteran whose narrative has been written for years, and one trying to rewrite his. The rankings say both have work to do.

articles.title: Notre Dame is national championship pick for Kirk Herbstreit, others
articles.summary: Four out of 20 major college football pundits have picked Notre Dame to win it all.
articles.body:
More than a few experts are picking the Notre Dame Fighting Irish as their 2026-2027 national champion.

David Cone, Kirk Herbstreit, Joel Klatt and Will Compton all have the Irish as their picks to win it all.

See photos from Notre Dame football practice on August 7, 2026

On3 Sports gathered the picks of 20 pundits and analysts from around the game, and those four chose the Irish. That's the second-most for a given team -- six picked Oregon . Three picked Miami (FL), two each picked Ohio State and Texas , and Georgia , Indiana and LSU each got one pick.

Irish fans will be hoping those four pundits are correct.

articles.title: Penn State football team finally begins Matt Campbell era against Marshall
articles.summary: Matt Campbell has spent the last nine months assembling his first Penn State football roster and staff, laying his program’s foundation, creating its culture...
articles.body:
Matt Campbell has spent the last nine months assembling his first Penn State football roster and staff, laying his program's foundation, creating its culture and finally preparing for the first game.

It's been a whirlwind in many ways, barely allowing the 46-year-old Campbell to catch his breath.

But the season has finally arrived. Penn State begins the Matt Campbell era in earnest against three-touchdown underdog Marshall Saturday at 3:30 (TV-FS1) at Beaver Stadium.

Like the rest of us, Campbell will finally see the product resulting from all the work.

"I'm looking forward to seeing how we handle the challenges," he said. "You have a good Marshall football team. They're going to put us in challenging situations. How do we respond to that? How do we handle the crowd? How do we handle our own ego, our own leadership?

"I think there's so much we're going to learn about ourselves."

After he left Iowa State to take over the Nittany Lions, Campbell and his staff made experience and size priorities when they put together the roster. It includes 40 transfers (24 from Iowa State) and about 50 Penn State returners.

The 2026 Lions are more experienced with 21 players who started at least half of their teams' games last season. They're bigger on both sides of the ball because Campbell wants to have a physical team.

Penn State lost four starters on the offensive line, including first-round draft pick Vega Ioane. Anthony Donkoh, the lone returning starter, moves back to right tackle after playing last season at guard.

Brock Riker, a Freshman All-American last season at Texas State, will anchor the line at center. He'll be flanked at guard by Cooper Cousins and Iowa State transfer Trevor Buhr, who did not allow a sack last season while receiving All-Big 12 honorable mention.

"Just watching him (Riker) take control and lead us out there has been really impressive," Buhr said. "His communication and his violence at the point of attack is awesome. He's a ballplayer. He does everything well."

Malachi Goodman, once a four-star prospect from New Jersey, will start at left tackle after not seeing action last season as a true freshman at Penn State.

"He's really had a tremendous camp," Campbell said. "We're excited about the growth that he's made and the consistency that he's given our football team across the board."

Unlike the previous three seasons, when Kaytron Allen and Nick Singleton carried the backfield load, the Lions will use four running backs: Carson Hansen, James Peoples, Quinton Martin Jr. and Cam Wallace.

On defense, linebacker Tony Rojas and cornerback Audavion Collins have enjoyed impressive performances in fall camp. Both were starters last season at Penn State, Rojas for four games before his season-ending knee injury.

"I feel like the old Tony," Rojas said. " I'm super excited to get out there with the guys and play fast. I've had a very good camp and it's been exciting."

Collins, one of the fastest players on the team, started every game last season and had 47 tackles and three pass breakups.

"He's really talented," quarterback Rocco Becht said. "He's really good at playing in between two different routes. He's really good at reading your eyes. He's definitely been an asset to me."

Marshall allowed 30.3 points per game last season when it went 5-7. The Thundering Herd returns just three starters on defense and six on offense, including quarterback Carlos Del Rio-Wilson, who accounted for 23 touchdowns last season.

"First games are challenging no matter if you've been there for 10 years or this is your first time around," Campbell said. "First games are always tricky and always challenging. I'm excited to get into this moment because it's going to tell us a lot more."

The Nittany Lions finally begin the Matt Campbell era and want to pound the football regardless of their opponent. The Thundering Herd will test the defense with its dual-threat QB, but expect Penn State to pull away with its depth.
